answer: A marketplace can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed if the same credential is reused, like a cipher key that unlocks only one door. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, while a legitimate agent pays once and earns it back through honest trades. Picture a wharf that charges every ship a berthing fee: one vessel passes cheaply, but a fleet of phantom ships bankrupts its owner before it can dock. A public marble ledger records each deposit, so duplicates are visible and cheap to challenge.
